sql:
-- ============================================================================
-- User tags
-- A tagging system for users. `tags` holds reusable tag definitions; `user_tags`
-- links a user to a tag. Tags are assigned automatically (e.g. a plan-name tag
-- when a subscription becomes active — written by the Stripe webhook with the
-- service role) and managed manually by staff (via a server-only admin endpoint
-- that also uses the service role). Regular users may only READ their own tags.
-- ============================================================================

create table public.tags (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  name text not null unique,
  color text, -- optional hex/utility color for the badge
  -- System tags are managed by the app (e.g. plan-name tags from billing) and
  -- shouldn't be hand-edited/deleted in the admin UI.
  is_system boolean not null default false,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now()
);

create table public.user_tags (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id uuid not null references public.profiles (id) on delete cascade,
  tag_id uuid not null references public.tags (id) on delete cascade,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  unique (user_id, tag_id)
);
-- FK indexes (every FK used in an RLS predicate / join needs one).
create index on public.user_tags (user_id);
create index on public.user_tags (tag_id);

alter table public.tags enable row level security;
alter table public.user_tags enable row level security;

-- Tag definitions are readable by any signed-in user (so the app can render a
-- user's tag names/colors). Writes are service-role only (no policy granted).
create policy "tags: read for authenticated"
  on public.tags for select to authenticated
  using (true);

-- A user may read only their own tag links. Writes are service-role only
-- (the webhook auto-tags by plan; staff manage tags via an admin endpoint).
create policy "user_tags: select own"
  on public.user_tags for select to authenticated
  using (user_id = (select auth.uid()));

-- service-role client (which bypasses RLS) reads/writes them. This is the

  channel       text not null,
  contact_key   text not null,

name: mcp_oauth
sql:
-- MCP remote server · OAuth 2.1 authorization-server storage.
--
-- The web app hosts a remote MCP server (packages/mcp) that an admin connects
-- from Claude/ChatGPT/Cursor. Auth follows the MCP authorization spec: the app
-- acts as its own OAuth 2.1 authorization server (dynamic client registration +
-- PKCE), reusing the existing Supabase /sign-in for the actual login.
--
-- These three tables hold that OAuth state. They are SERVER-ONLY: the only
-- principal that touches them is the app's service-role client (golden rule #2),
-- never an RLS browser/mobile client. So RLS is enabled with NO policies
-- (deny-all to anon/authenticated; service_role has BYPASSRLS), and table
-- privileges are revoked from anon/authenticated and the payload_cms role.
-- Access tokens are stateless signed JWTs (verified with MCP_JWT_SECRET, no DB
-- hit) — only refresh tokens (rotating, hashed) and authorization codes persist.

-- Registered MCP clients (RFC 7591 Dynamic Client Registration). Public PKCE
-- clients are the norm (token_endpoint_auth_method = 'none', no secret).
create table if not exists public.mcp_oauth_clients (
  id text primary key,
  client_secret_hash text,
  client_name text,
  redirect_uris text[] not null,
  grant_types text[] not null default '{authorization_code,refresh_token}',
  token_endpoint_auth_method text not null default 'none',
  scope text,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now()
);

-- Single-use, short-lived (~60s) authorization codes bound to a staff user and
-- a PKCE challenge. Consumed exactly once at the token endpoint.
create table if not exists public.mcp_authorization_codes (
  code text primary key,
  client_id text not null references public.mcp_oauth_clients (id) on delete cascade,
  supabase_user_id uuid not null references public.profiles (id) on delete cascade,
  redirect_uri text not null,
  code_challenge text not null,
  code_challenge_method text not null default 'S256',
  scope text,
  expires_at timestamptz not null,
  consumed_at timestamptz,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now()
);
create index if not exists mcp_authorization_codes_expires_idx
  on public.mcp_authorization_codes (expires_at);

-- Rotating refresh tokens. We store only the SHA-256 hash of the opaque token;
-- on use we rotate (issue a new token, set rotated_to, revoke the old). A replay
-- of an already-rotated token is reuse — revoke the whole chain.
create table if not exists public.mcp_refresh_tokens (
  token_hash text primary key,
  client_id text not null references public.mcp_oauth_clients (id) on delete cascade,
  supabase_user_id uuid not null references public.profiles (id) on delete cascade,
  scope text,
  expires_at timestamptz not null,
  rotated_to text,
  revoked_at timestamptz,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now()
);
create index if not exists mcp_refresh_tokens_user_idx
  on public.mcp_refresh_tokens (supabase_user_id);

-- Deny-all RLS: enabled, no policies. Only the service-role key (BYPASSRLS)
-- reaches these rows; anon/authenticated get nothing.
alter table public.mcp_oauth_clients enable row level security;
alter table public.mcp_authorization_codes enable row level security;
alter table public.mcp_refresh_tokens enable row level security;

-- Defense in depth: strip table privileges from the RLS roles and from the
-- least-privilege Payload role (which must never see `public`).
revoke all on public.mcp_oauth_clients from anon, authenticated;
revoke all on public.mcp_authorization_codes from anon, authenticated;
revoke all on public.mcp_refresh_tokens from anon, authenticated;

do $$
begin
  if exists (select 1 from pg_roles where rolname = 'payload_cms') then
    revoke all on public.mcp_oauth_clients from payload_cms;
    revoke all on public.mcp_authorization_codes from payload_cms;
    revoke all on public.mcp_refresh_tokens from payload_cms;
  end if;
end
$$;

name: anon_identity
sql:
-- Anonymous-account-first identity + checkout linking.
--
-- Gives every visitor a real auth.uid() early (a Supabase anonymous user, minted
-- on first action — e.g. favoriting any content), so checkout always links to an
-- account and converts to a permanent user once an email is known. See
-- docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and docs/TURNSTILE.md. Append-only + idempotent-friendly.
--
-- Sections: profiles (anon flag, phone) · handle_new_user guard · content_favorites
-- (the one table anon users may write) · anon-exclusion on cost-bearing AI tables.

-- ============================================================================
-- profiles: track anonymity + capture phone from wallet checkout
-- ============================================================================

alter table public.profiles
  add column if not exists is_anonymous boolean not null default false;
alter table public.profiles
  add column if not exists phone text;

comment on column public.profiles.is_anonymous is
  'True for Supabase anonymous users (minted on first action). Never staff; converted to permanent on email confirmation.';

-- Let owners save their phone (captured from Apple/Google Pay) — same column-level
-- grant pattern as display_name/avatar_url. is_staff/is_anonymous stay server-only.
grant update (phone) on public.profiles to authenticated;

-- handle_new_user, hardened for anonymous users: an anon signup is NEVER staff,
-- and the "first user becomes founder/admin" rule counts only NON-anonymous
-- profiles (so a bot's anonymous sign-in can't claim the founder slot).
create or replace function public.handle_new_user()
returns trigger
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = ''
as $$
begin
  insert into public.profiles (id, display_name, avatar_url, is_anonymous, is_staff)
  values (
    new.id,
    coalesce(
      new.raw_user_meta_data ->> 'display_name',
      new.raw_user_meta_data ->> 'name',
      split_part(coalesce(new.email, ''), '@', 1)
    ),
    new.raw_user_meta_data ->> 'avatar_url',
    coalesce(new.is_anonymous, false),
    -- First NON-anonymous profile becomes staff (the founder/admin); anon never.
    (not coalesce(new.is_anonymous, false))
      and (select count(*) = 0 from public.profiles where is_anonymous = false)
  )
  on conflict (id) do nothing;
  return new;
end;
$$;

-- ============================================================================
-- content_favorites: per-user saves across ALL content collections. The ONLY
-- table anonymous users may write. Content lives in the cms schema, so the item
-- is referenced by its Payload collection slug + doc id (no FK).
-- ============================================================================

create table if not exists public.content_favorites (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id uuid not null references auth.users (id) on delete cascade,
  collection text not null,            -- Payload collection slug (posts/videos/audio/…)
  item_id text not null,               -- content doc id (cms schema → no FK)
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  unique (user_id, collection, item_id)
);
create index if not exists content_favorites_user_id_idx
  on public.content_favorites (user_id);

alter table public.content_favorites enable row level security;

drop policy if exists "content_favorites: own" on public.content_favorites;
create policy "content_favorites: own"
  on public.content_favorites for all to authenticated
  using (user_id = (select auth.uid()))
  with check (user_id = (select auth.uid()));

-- ============================================================================
-- Anon-exclusion on cost-bearing AI tables (defense in depth).
-- Anonymous users carry role=authenticated, so they'd otherwise inherit the
-- existing "own" policies on the AI chat tables and could burn AI compute.
-- A RESTRICTIVE policy is AND-ed with the permissive ones, so it blocks anon
-- writes/reads regardless of how the chat policies evolve. The AI route should
-- also reject anon sessions server-side.
-- ============================================================================

drop policy if exists "ext_chat_threads: no anon" on public.ext_chat_threads;
create policy "ext_chat_threads: no anon"
  on public.ext_chat_threads as restrictive for all to authenticated
  using (coalesce(((select auth.jwt()) ->> 'is_anonymous')::boolean, false) = false)
  with check (coalesce(((select auth.jwt()) ->> 'is_anonymous')::boolean, false) = false);

drop policy if exists "ext_chat_messages: no anon" on public.ext_chat_messages;
create policy "ext_chat_messages: no anon"
  on public.ext_chat_messages as restrictive for all to authenticated
  using (coalesce(((select auth.jwt()) ->> 'is_anonymous')::boolean, false) = false)
  with check (coalesce(((select auth.jwt()) ->> 'is_anonymous')::boolean, false) = false);

name: anon_block_cost_tables
sql:
-- Extend the anonymous-write block to the remaining cost- / notification-bearing
-- tables (golden rule #1: content_favorites is the ONLY table anon users may write).
--
-- 20260624000000_anon_identity.sql added a RESTRICTIVE "no anon" policy to
-- ext_chat_threads + ext_chat_messages, but the other AI-chat SDK tables plus the
-- reminders + notifications tables and the core `files` table still carried only
-- their permissive `for all to authenticated` owner policies. Anonymous users
-- hold role=authenticated, so they inherited those and could write rows —
-- notably ext_reminders / ext_notifications_push_tokens, which are
-- push-notification-bearing and were the substrate for unconsented data grafting
-- via anon reconciliation.
--
-- A RESTRICTIVE policy is AND-ed with the permissive ones, so it blocks anon
-- reads/writes regardless of how each table's owner policy evolves. Append-only,
-- idempotent (drop-if-exists), and guarded by to_regclass so removing an
-- extension (which drops its tables) can't break this migration.

do $$
declare
  t text;
  tables text[] := array[
    -- reminders + notifications (push-bearing / user-owned state)
    'ext_reminders',
    'ext_notifications',
    'ext_notifications_push_tokens',
    -- remaining AI-chat SDK tables (threads + messages already blocked)
    'ext_chat_documents',
    'ext_chat_suggestions',
    'ext_chat_votes',
    -- core user uploads (storage-bearing)
    'files'
  ];
begin
  foreach t in array tables loop
    if to_regclass('public.' || t) is not null then
      execute format('drop policy if exists %I on public.%I', t || ': no anon', t);
      execute format(
        'create policy %I on public.%I as restrictive for all to authenticated '
        'using (coalesce(((select auth.jwt()) ->> ''is_anonymous'')::boolean, false) = false) '
        'with check (coalesce(((select auth.jwt()) ->> ''is_anonymous'')::boolean, false) = false)',
        t || ': no anon', t
      );
    end if;
  end loop;
end $$;

name: mod_billing_002_rename_to_mod_prefix
sql:
-- Modules used to be called "extensions", and their tables used the
-- `ext_` prefix. Rename this module's tables to `mod_*`, then rename the
-- constraints, indexes and RLS policies on them that still carry the old
-- prefix. Renames keep data, grants, RLS and foreign keys intact. Idempotent:
-- a no-op where the rename already happened.
alter table if exists public.ext_billing_customers rename to mod_billing_customers;
alter table if exists public.ext_billing_products rename to mod_billing_products;
alter table if exists public.ext_billing_prices rename to mod_billing_prices;
alter table if exists public.ext_billing_subscriptions rename to mod_billing_subscriptions;

do $$
declare
  own text[] := array['mod_billing_customers', 'mod_billing_products', 'mod_billing_prices', 'mod_billing_subscriptions'];
  r record;
begin
  for r in
    select t.relname as tbl, c.conname as name
    from pg_constraint c
    join pg_class t on t.oid = c.conrelid
    join pg_namespace n on n.oid = t.relnamespace
    where n.nspname = 'public' and t.relname = any (own) and c.conname like 'ext\_%'
  loop
    execute format('alter table %I.%I rename constraint %I to %I',
      'public', r.tbl, r.name, 'mod_' || substr(r.name, 5));
  end loop;

  for r in
    select i.relname as name
    from pg_index x
    join pg_class i on i.oid = x.indexrelid
    join pg_class t on t.oid = x.indrelid
    join pg_namespace n on n.oid = t.relnamespace
    where n.nspname = 'public' and t.relname = any (own) and i.relname like 'ext\_%'
  loop
    execute format('alter index %I.%I rename to %I',
      'public', r.name, 'mod_' || substr(r.name, 5));
  end loop;

  for r in
    select t.relname as tbl, p.polname as name
    from pg_policy p
    join pg_class t on t.oid = p.polrelid
    join pg_namespace n on n.oid = t.relnamespace
    where n.nspname = 'public' and t.relname = any (own) and p.polname like 'ext\_%'
  loop
    execute format('alter policy %I on %I.%I rename to %I',
      r.name, 'public', r.tbl, 'mod_' || substr(r.name, 5));
  end loop;
end
$$;

sql:
-- Notifications 1.1 · the producer contract.
--
-- Other modules (CRM, client portal, …) PRODUCE notifications; this module
-- DELIVERS them. Producers describe what happened and how each channel should
-- render it; they never send email or push themselves. Today delivery is the
-- in-app feed (plus Expo push from the TypeScript notify() path). Email, web
-- push, preferences and a delivery queue are added inside this module later,
-- behind the same contract, so producers don't change.
--
-- What this migration adds (all additive, reattach-friendly):
--   * mod_notifications: category, source_module, url, entity_type/entity_id,
--     actor_id, channels, payload (per-channel renderings), dedupe_key.
--   * mod_notifications_categories: producers register the categories they
--     emit (from their own migrations), so a future preferences screen can
--     list them with a label, audience and default channels.
--   * mod_notifications_emit(...): the one SQL entry point for producers'
--     triggers and definer functions.

-- ============================================================================
-- Contract columns
-- ============================================================================

alter table public.mod_notifications
  add column if not exists category text,
  add column if not exists source_module text,
  add column if not exists url text,
  add column if not exists entity_type text,
  add column if not exists entity_id text,
  add column if not exists actor_id uuid references public.profiles (id) on delete set null,
  add column if not exists channels text[],
  add column if not exists payload jsonb not null default '{}'::jsonb,
  add column if not exists dedupe_key text;

-- Channels a producer may request. `in_app` is the feed; the others are
-- delivered once this module grows those channels.
alter table public.mod_notifications
  drop constraint if exists mod_notifications_channels_check;
alter table public.mod_notifications
  add constraint mod_notifications_channels_check
  check (channels is null or channels <@ array['in_app', 'push', 'web_push', 'email', 'sms']::text[]);

-- Click-through targets: an app path ("/a/…") or an https URL — never
-- javascript:, data: or protocol-relative ("//evil.example") links.
alter table public.mod_notifications
  drop constraint if exists mod_notifications_url_check;
alter table public.mod_notifications
  add constraint mod_notifications_url_check
  check (url is null or url ~ '^(/($|[^/\\])|https://)');

alter table public.mod_notifications
  drop constraint if exists mod_notifications_payload_check;
alter table public.mod_notifications
  add constraint mod_notifications_payload_check
  check (jsonb_typeof(payload) = 'object');

-- One notification per (user, dedupe_key): producers pass a stable key
-- ("case-comment:<id>") so a retried trigger or route never notifies twice.
create unique index if not exists mod_notifications_dedupe_idx
  on public.mod_notifications (user_id, dedupe_key)
  where dedupe_key is not null;

create index if not exists mod_notifications_user_created_idx
  on public.mod_notifications (user_id, created_at desc);

-- ============================================================================
-- Category registry
-- ============================================================================

create table if not exists public.mod_notifications_categories (
  -- "<module>.<thing>[.<event>]", e.g. "client-portal.case.reply".
  key text primary key
    check (key ~ '^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*(\.[a-z0-9_-]+)+$'),
  module text not null,
  label text not null,
  description text,
  -- Who receives it: product users (client), staff, or anyone.
  audience text not null default 'everyone'
    check (audience in ('client', 'staff', 'everyone')),
  default_channels text[] not null default array['in_app', 'push']::text[]
    check (default_channels <@ array['in_app', 'push', 'web_push', 'email', 'sms']::text[]),
  -- Transactional notifications (security, receipts, direct replies) can't
  -- be switched off entirely by a future preferences screen.
  transactional boolean not null default false,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  updated_at timestamptz not null default now()
);

alter table public.mod_notifications_categories enable row level security;

-- Readable by signed-in users (a preferences screen lists them). No write
-- policy: rows are written by module migrations (the table owner) only.
drop policy if exists "mod_notifications_categories: read" on public.mod_notifications_categories;
create policy "mod_notifications_categories: read"
  on public.mod_notifications_categories for select to authenticated
  using (true);

drop policy if exists "mod_notifications_categories: no anon" on public.mod_notifications_categories;
create policy "mod_notifications_categories: no anon"
  on public.mod_notifications_categories as restrictive for all to anon
  using (false);

-- Producers register categories with this upsert so a module update can
-- change a label without a conflict error.
create or replace function public.mod_notifications_register_category(
  _key text,
  _module text,
  _label text,
  _description text default null,
  _audience text default 'everyone',
  _default_channels text[] default array['in_app', 'push']::text[],
  _transactional boolean default false
)
returns void
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = ''
as $$
begin
  -- Only system code (migrations, service role) registers categories.
  if coalesce((select auth.role()), '') in ('authenticated', 'anon') then
    raise exception 'mod_notifications_register_category: not allowed'
      using errcode = '42501';
  end if;
  insert into public.mod_notifications_categories
    (key, module, label, description, audience, default_channels, transactional)
  values (_key, _module, _label, _description, _audience,
          coalesce(_default_channels, array['in_app', 'push']::text[]),
          coalesce(_transactional, false))
  on conflict (key) do update
    set module = excluded.module,
        label = excluded.label,
        description = excluded.description,
        audience = excluded.audience,
        default_channels = excluded.default_channels,
        transactional = excluded.transactional,
        updated_at = now();
end;
$$;

-- ============================================================================
-- mod_notifications_emit — the producer entry point
-- ============================================================================
--
-- Inserts one notification and returns its id (null when the dedupe key was
-- already used, or when _user is null). Allowed callers:
--   * a trigger (pg_trigger_depth() > 0) — producers' row triggers;
--   * system code: the service role, or a session with no JWT (cron, edge
--     functions using the SQL contract, migrations);
--   * a producer's definer function that set the transaction-local flag
--     `mod_notifications.emit = 'on'` (clients can't set GUCs over PostgREST);
--   * anyone notifying themself (the feed's own RLS already allows that).
-- A signed-in client calling it directly for someone else is refused, so the
-- RPC can't be used to spam other users.
--
-- The future delivery fan-out (deliveries queue, email, web push, user
-- preferences) hangs off this function and the row it writes.
create or replace function public.mod_notifications_emit(
  _user uuid,
  _category text,
  _title text default null,
  _body text default null,
  _url text default null,
  _entity_type text default null,
  _entity_id text default null,
  _channels text[] default null,
  _payload jsonb default '{}'::jsonb,
  _dedupe_key text default null,
  _actor uuid default null,
  _source_module text default null,
  _data jsonb default '{}'::jsonb
)
returns uuid
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = ''
as $$
declare
  _id uuid;
begin
  if _user is null or _category is null then
    return null;
  end if;
  -- coalesce(..., false): any NULL in the checks (anon has no auth.uid())
  -- must refuse, never fall through.
  if not coalesce(
    pg_trigger_depth() > 0
    or coalesce(current_setting('mod_notifications.emit', true), '') = 'on'
    or coalesce((select auth.role()), '') not in ('authenticated', 'anon')
    or _user is not distinct from (select auth.uid()),
    false
  ) then
    raise exception 'mod_notifications_emit: not allowed' using errcode = '42501';
  end if;

  insert into public.mod_notifications (
    user_id, type, category, source_module, title, body, url,
    entity_type, entity_id, actor_id, channels, payload, dedupe_key, data
  )
  values (
    _user,
    _category,
    _category,
    coalesce(_source_module, split_part(_category, '.', 1)),
    _title,
    _body,
    _url,
    _entity_type,
    _entity_id,
    _actor,
    _channels,
    coalesce(_payload, '{}'::jsonb),
    _dedupe_key,
    -- Keep data.url for readers written before the url column existed.
    coalesce(_data, '{}'::jsonb)
      || case when _url is not null then jsonb_build_object('url', _url) else '{}'::jsonb end
  )
  on conflict (user_id, dedupe_key) where dedupe_key is not null do nothing
  returning id into _id;

  return _id;
end;
$$;

-- A producer's drop.sql removes its categories with this (no DML whitelist
-- needed on this module's tables). Past notifications are kept.
create or replace function public.mod_notifications_unregister_module(_module text)
returns void
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = ''
as $$
begin
  if coalesce((select auth.role()), '') in ('authenticated', 'anon') then
    raise exception 'mod_notifications_unregister_module: not allowed'
      using errcode = '42501';
  end if;
  delete from public.mod_notifications_categories where module = _module;
end;
$$;

name: founder_not_exists
sql:
-- handle_new_user(): constant-time founder check, race-safe.
--
-- The previous version ran `select count(*) = 0 from profiles where
-- is_anonymous = false` on EVERY signup — a full count that grows with the
-- user base — and two concurrent first signups could both see zero and both
-- become staff. Now:
--   * `not exists` over a partial index on permanent profiles (O(1) once any
--     permanent profile exists);
--   * only when that says "no founder yet" do we take a transaction-scoped
--     advisory lock and re-check, so concurrent first signups serialize and
--     exactly one becomes the founder. Every later signup skips the lock.
-- Behaviour is otherwise unchanged (anon users are never staff; email mirror).
-- Append-only + idempotent-friendly.

create index if not exists profiles_permanent_created_idx
  on public.profiles (created_at)
  where not is_anonymous;

create or replace function public.handle_new_user()
returns trigger
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = ''
as $$
declare
  _is_anon boolean := coalesce(new.is_anonymous, false);
  _founder boolean := false;
begin
  if not _is_anon
     and not exists (select 1 from public.profiles p where not p.is_anonymous) then
    perform pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('public.handle_new_user:founder'));
    -- Re-check under the lock: a concurrent first signup may have committed.
    _founder := not exists (select 1 from public.profiles p where not p.is_anonymous);
  end if;

  insert into public.profiles (id, display_name, avatar_url, is_anonymous, is_staff, email)
  values (
    new.id,
    coalesce(
      new.raw_user_meta_data ->> 'display_name',
      new.raw_user_meta_data ->> 'name',
      split_part(coalesce(new.email, ''), '@', 1)
    ),
    new.raw_user_meta_data ->> 'avatar_url',
    _is_anon,
    -- First NON-anonymous profile becomes staff (the founder/admin); anon never.
    _founder,
    nullif(new.email, '')
  )
  on conflict (id) do nothing;
  return new;
end;
$$;

name: mod_notifications_004_delivery_fixes
sql:
-- Notifications 1.2 · delivery fixes.
--
-- 1. Push tokens are unique per DEVICE (token), not per (user, token). A
--    shared or re-logged-in device used to stay registered to every account
--    that ever used it, so it received other users' pushes. Registration now
--    goes through mod_notifications_register_push_token(), which moves the
--    token to the caller.
-- 2. Broadcasts are set-based. The dispatcher used to read `profiles` and
--    push tokens through PostgREST, which silently stops at `max_rows`
--    (1000), and it included anonymous users. mod_notifications_broadcast()
--    inserts the in-app rows in one statement, and
--    mod_notifications_audience_tokens() pages tokens with a keyset cursor.
--    Both refuse signed-in and anonymous callers (service role / no JWT only);
--    module SQL can't GRANT or REVOKE, so each function checks its caller.
--
-- Reattach-friendly (if not exists / drop-then-create / or replace).

-- ============================================================================
-- 1. One row per device token
-- ============================================================================

-- Keep the newest registration of each token before adding the constraint.
delete from public.mod_notifications_push_tokens t
using public.mod_notifications_push_tokens newer
where t.token = newer.token
  and (t.created_at, t.id) < (newer.created_at, newer.id);

do $$
begin
  if not exists (
    select 1 from pg_constraint
    where conname = 'mod_notifications_push_tokens_token_key'
  ) then
    alter table public.mod_notifications_push_tokens
      add constraint mod_notifications_push_tokens_token_key unique (token);
  end if;
end;
$$;

-- The old (user_id, token) key is now redundant (token alone is unique).
-- Its name depends on whether the table predates the ext_ → mod_ rename.
alter table public.mod_notifications_push_tokens
  drop constraint if exists mod_notifications_push_tokens_user_id_token_key;
alter table public.mod_notifications_push_tokens
  drop constraint if exists ext_notifications_push_tokens_user_id_token_key;

-- Register (or move) the calling device's token to the caller.
create or replace function public.mod_notifications_register_push_token(
  _token text,
  _platform text
)
returns void
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = ''
as $$
begin
  if (select auth.uid()) is null or public.is_anonymous_session() then
    raise exception 'not_allowed' using errcode = 'P0001';
  end if;
  if _token is null or char_length(_token) not between 1 and 512 then
    raise exception 'invalid_token' using errcode = 'P0001';
  end if;
  if _platform not in ('ios', 'android', 'web') then
    raise exception 'invalid_platform' using errcode = 'P0001';
  end if;
  insert into public.mod_notifications_push_tokens (user_id, token, platform)
  values ((select auth.uid()), _token, _platform)
  on conflict (token) do update
    set user_id = excluded.user_id,
        platform = excluded.platform,
        created_at = now();
end;
$$;

-- ============================================================================
-- 2. Set-based broadcast
-- ============================================================================

-- Audience: 'all' (every permanent user), 'users' (_user_ids) or 'tags'
-- (users carrying any of _tag_names). Anonymous users are never included.
create or replace function public.mod_notifications_audience(
  _audience text,
  _user_ids uuid[] default null,
  _tag_names text[] default null
)
returns table (user_id uuid)
language plpgsql
stable
security definer
set search_path = ''
as $$
begin
  -- System callers only (service role, or no JWT). Module SQL can't GRANT or
  -- REVOKE, so every service-only function checks its caller itself.
  if coalesce((select auth.role()), '') in ('authenticated', 'anon') then
    raise exception 'mod_notifications_audience: not allowed' using errcode = '42501';
  end if;
  return query
    select p.id
    from public.profiles p
    where not p.is_anonymous
      and case _audience
        when 'all' then true
        when 'users' then p.id = any (coalesce(_user_ids, '{}'))
        when 'tags' then exists (
          select 1
          from public.user_tags ut
          join public.tags t on t.id = ut.tag_id
          where ut.user_id = p.id and t.name = any (coalesce(_tag_names, '{}'))
        )
        else false
      end;
end;
$$;

-- Insert one in-app notification per audience member. Idempotent per
-- (user, _dedupe_key), so a retried broadcast never duplicates rows.
-- Returns the number of rows inserted.
create or replace function public.mod_notifications_broadcast(
  _dedupe_key text,
  _category text,
  _title text default null,
  _body text default null,
  _url text default null,
  _data jsonb default '{}'::jsonb,
  _audience text default 'all',
  _user_ids uuid[] default null,
  _tag_names text[] default null,
  _source_module text default null
)
returns integer
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = ''
as $$
declare
  _inserted integer;
begin
  -- System callers only (service role, or no JWT: cron / migrations).
  if coalesce((select auth.role()), '') in ('authenticated', 'anon') then
    raise exception 'mod_notifications_broadcast: not allowed' using errcode = '42501';
  end if;
  if _dedupe_key is null or _category is null then
    raise exception 'mod_notifications_broadcast: dedupe key and category are required'
      using errcode = '22023';
  end if;

  insert into public.mod_notifications (
    user_id, type, category, source_module, title, body, url, data, dedupe_key
  )
  select
    a.user_id,
    _category,
    _category,
    coalesce(_source_module, split_part(_category, '.', 1)),
    _title,
    _body,
    _url,
    coalesce(_data, '{}'::jsonb)
      || case when _url is not null then jsonb_build_object('url', _url) else '{}'::jsonb end,
    _dedupe_key
  from public.mod_notifications_audience(_audience, _user_ids, _tag_names) a
  on conflict (user_id, dedupe_key) where dedupe_key is not null do nothing;

  get diagnostics _inserted = row_count;
  return _inserted;
end;
$$;

-- Page through the audience's push tokens: pass the last id you got as
-- _after (null for the first page). Ordered by id for a stable keyset. The
-- audience predicate is written out here rather than calling
-- mod_notifications_audience(): a security-definer function can't be inlined,
-- so every page would otherwise rebuild the whole audience.
create or replace function public.mod_notifications_audience_tokens(
  _audience text,
  _user_ids uuid[] default null,
  _tag_names text[] default null,
  _after uuid default null,
  _limit integer default 500
)
returns table (id uuid, token text)
language plpgsql
stable
security definer
set search_path = ''
as $$
begin
  if coalesce((select auth.role()), '') in ('authenticated', 'anon') then
    raise exception 'mod_notifications_audience_tokens: not allowed' using errcode = '42501';
  end if;
  return query
    select t.id, t.token
    from public.mod_notifications_push_tokens t
    join public.profiles p on p.id = t.user_id
    where not p.is_anonymous
      and (_after is null or t.id > _after)
      and case _audience
        when 'all' then true
        when 'users' then t.user_id = any (coalesce(_user_ids, '{}'))
        when 'tags' then exists (
          select 1
          from public.user_tags ut
          join public.tags tg on tg.id = ut.tag_id
          where ut.user_id = t.user_id and tg.name = any (coalesce(_tag_names, '{}'))
        )
        else false
      end
    order by t.id
    limit least(greatest(coalesce(_limit, 500), 1), 1000);
end;
$$;

name: mod_reminders_003_claim
sql:
-- Reminders 1.1 · safe, bounded delivery.
--
-- The processor used to select EVERY due reminder (no limit, silently capped
-- at PostgREST's max_rows), deliver them one by one, and mark them sent
-- afterwards — two overlapping runs sent everything twice, and a crash left
-- nothing to retry. mod_reminders_claim() hands out a bounded batch with
-- `for update skip locked`, marks it 'processing', and re-offers rows a
-- crashed worker left behind (up to 5 attempts). It refuses signed-in and
-- anonymous callers (module SQL can't GRANT/REVOKE, so it checks itself).
--
-- Reattach-friendly (if not exists / drop-then-create / or replace).

alter table public.mod_reminders
  add column if not exists attempts integer not null default 0,
  add column if not exists claimed_at timestamptz;

-- Allow the new 'processing' state. The inline check's name depends on
-- whether the table predates the ext_ → mod_ rename.
alter table public.mod_reminders drop constraint if exists ext_reminders_status_check;
alter table public.mod_reminders drop constraint if exists mod_reminders_status_check;
alter table public.mod_reminders
  add constraint mod_reminders_status_check
  check (status in ('pending', 'processing', 'sent', 'canceled'));

-- The scheduler only ever looks at due pending rows and stuck claims, so
-- partial indexes keep both scans small no matter how much history builds up.
drop index if exists public.mod_reminders_status_due_at_idx;
drop index if exists public.ext_reminders_status_due_at_idx;
create index if not exists mod_reminders_pending_due_idx
  on public.mod_reminders (due_at)
  where status = 'pending';
create index if not exists mod_reminders_processing_claimed_idx
  on public.mod_reminders (claimed_at)
  where status = 'processing';

create or replace function public.mod_reminders_claim(
  _limit integer default 100,
  _stale_after interval default interval '10 minutes'
)
returns table (id uuid, user_id uuid, channel text, attempts integer)
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = ''
as $$
begin
  if coalesce((select auth.role()), '') in ('authenticated', 'anon') then
    raise exception 'mod_reminders_claim: not allowed' using errcode = '42501';
  end if;
  return query
    update public.mod_reminders r
       set status = 'processing',
           claimed_at = now(),
           attempts = r.attempts + 1
     where r.id in (
       select c.id
       from public.mod_reminders c
       where (c.status = 'pending' and c.due_at <= now())
          or (c.status = 'processing'
              and c.claimed_at < now() - _stale_after
              and c.attempts < 5)
       order by c.due_at
       for update skip locked
       limit least(greatest(coalesce(_limit, 100), 1), 1000)
     )
    returning r.id, r.user_id, r.channel, r.attempts;
end;
$$;

name: rls_initplan_and_indexes
sql:
-- Scale hardening · workspace RLS evaluated once per query + index hygiene.
-- docs/ERD.md (RLS & ownership model), docs/WORKSPACES.md.
--
-- 1. Org-scoped policies used `public.is_org_member(org_id)` /
--    `is_org_admin(org_id)`. Those are SECURITY DEFINER, so Postgres can't
--    inline them, and because they take a row column they run once PER ROW.
--    The Supabase-documented pattern is `org_id = any (array(select
--    <set-returning definer fn>()))`: the function doesn't depend on the row,
--    so it runs once per statement (an InitPlan), and the array comparison
--    lets the planner use the primary-key / unique indexes.
--    The helpers live in a `private` schema that PostgREST does NOT expose
--    (Supabase: never put security-definer helpers in an exposed schema).
--    The public is_org_member()/is_org_admin() RPCs stay for clients and RPCs.
-- 2. Indexes: cover the helper's lookup, index the remaining FK columns that
--    ON DELETE actions scan, and drop indexes a unique key already covers.
-- 3. workspace_members() pages with a keyset cursor (it used to return every
--    member, which PostgREST silently cut at max_rows).
--
-- Append-only + idempotent-friendly.

-- ============================================================================
-- 1. private helpers + org-scoped policies
-- ============================================================================

create schema if not exists private;
revoke all on schema private from public;
grant usage on schema private to authenticated, service_role;

comment on schema private is
  'Security-definer helpers used by RLS policies. Not exposed through the Data API.';

-- Workspaces the caller belongs to / administers.
create or replace function private.user_org_ids()
returns setof uuid
language sql
stable
security definer
set search_path = ''
as $$
  select m.org_id
  from public.memberships m
  where m.user_id = (select auth.uid());
$$;

create or replace function private.user_admin_org_ids()
returns setof uuid
language sql
stable
security definer
set search_path = ''
as $$
  select m.org_id
  from public.memberships m
  where m.user_id = (select auth.uid())
    and m.role in ('owner', 'admin');
$$;

revoke all on function private.user_org_ids() from public, anon;
revoke all on function private.user_admin_org_ids() from public, anon;
grant execute on function private.user_org_ids() to authenticated, service_role;
grant execute on function private.user_admin_org_ids() to authenticated, service_role;

-- organizations
drop policy if exists "orgs: select if member" on public.organizations;
create policy "orgs: select if member"
  on public.organizations for select to authenticated
  using (
    owner_id = (select auth.uid())
    or id = any (array(select private.user_org_ids()))
  );

-- memberships
drop policy if exists "memberships: select if member" on public.memberships;
create policy "memberships: select if member"
  on public.memberships for select to authenticated
  using (org_id = any (array(select private.user_org_ids())));

drop policy if exists "memberships: admins insert" on public.memberships;
create policy "memberships: admins insert"
  on public.memberships for insert to authenticated
  with check (org_id = any (array(select private.user_admin_org_ids())));

drop policy if exists "memberships: admins update" on public.memberships;
create policy "memberships: admins update"
  on public.memberships for update to authenticated
  using (org_id = any (array(select private.user_admin_org_ids())))
  with check (org_id = any (array(select private.user_admin_org_ids())));

drop policy if exists "memberships: admins delete" on public.memberships;
create policy "memberships: admins delete"
  on public.memberships for delete to authenticated
  using (org_id = any (array(select private.user_admin_org_ids())));

-- invitations
drop policy if exists "invitations: admins all" on public.invitations;
create policy "invitations: admins all"
  on public.invitations for all to authenticated
  using (org_id = any (array(select private.user_admin_org_ids())))
  with check (org_id = any (array(select private.user_admin_org_ids())));

-- ============================================================================
-- 2. Indexes
-- ============================================================================

-- memberships: the helpers look up by user_id and read org_id + role — make
-- that an index-only scan. It supersedes the single-column user_id index; the
-- org_id index is a prefix of the (org_id, user_id) unique key.
create index if not exists memberships_user_org_role_idx
  on public.memberships (user_id, org_id) include (role);
drop index if exists public.memberships_user_id_idx;
drop index if exists public.memberships_org_id_idx;

-- profiles.last_org_id: ON DELETE SET NULL from organizations scans profiles
-- without it.
create index if not exists profiles_last_org_id_idx
  on public.profiles (last_org_id)
  where last_org_id is not null;

-- invitations: SET NULL FKs to profiles, and the 50/day rate-limit count.
create index if not exists invitations_invited_by_idx

-- ============================================================================
-- 3. workspace_members(): keyset pages
-- ============================================================================

-- Same columns and order as before (owners, admins, members; then join date),
-- plus a stable tiebreak. Pass the last row's user_id as _after for the next
-- page. Defaults keep old one-argument callers working (first 1000 rows).
drop function if exists public.workspace_members(uuid);

create or replace function public.workspace_members(
  _org uuid,
  _limit integer default 1000,
  _after uuid default null
)
returns table (
  user_id uuid,
  display_name text,
  avatar_url text,
  title text,
  email text,
  role text,
  joined_at timestamptz,
  is_you boolean
)
language plpgsql
stable
security definer
set search_path = ''
as $$
declare
  _cursor_rank integer;
  _cursor_at timestamptz;
begin
  if not public.is_org_member(_org) then
    raise exception 'not_a_member' using errcode = 'P0001';
  end if;
  if _after is not null then
    select case c.role when 'owner' then 0 when 'admin' then 1 else 2 end, c.created_at
      into _cursor_rank, _cursor_at
    from public.memberships c
    where c.org_id = _org and c.user_id = _after;
  end if;
  return query
    select
      m.user_id,
      p.display_name,
      p.avatar_url,
      p.title,
      u.email::text,
      m.role,
      m.created_at,
      m.user_id = (select auth.uid())
    from public.memberships m
    join public.profiles p on p.id = m.user_id
    left join auth.users u on u.id = m.user_id
    where m.org_id = _org
      and (
        _cursor_rank is null
        or (case m.role when 'owner' then 0 when 'admin' then 1 else 2 end, m.created_at, m.user_id)
           > (_cursor_rank, _cursor_at, _after)
      )
    order by
      case m.role when 'owner' then 0 when 'admin' then 1 else 2 end,
      m.created_at,
      m.user_id
    limit least(greatest(coalesce(_limit, 1000), 1), 1000);
end;
$$;

grant execute on function public.workspace_members(uuid, integer, uuid) to authenticated;

-- * The feed used to fetch EVERY notification and count unread ones in the
--   client. It now reads one page (newest first, keyset on created_at, id)
--   and asks mod_notifications_unread_count(), served by a partial index that
--   only holds unread rows.
-- * mod_notifications_mark_all_read() marks the caller's feed read in one
--   statement.
-- * (user_id) is a prefix of (user_id, created_at desc) — dropped.
-- * actor_id is a SET NULL FK to profiles — indexed for profile deletes.
--
-- Both RPCs run as the caller (security invoker), so RLS still applies and
-- they also filter to the caller explicitly.
--
-- Reattach-friendly (if not exists / if exists / or replace).

  on public.mod_notifications (actor_id)
  where actor_id is not null;

returns integer
language sql
stable
security invoker
set search_path = ''
as $$
  select count(*)::integer
  from public.mod_notifications n
  where n.user_id = (select auth.uid())
    and n.read_at is null;
$$;

create or replace function public.mod_notifications_mark_all_read()
returns integer
language plpgsql
security invoker
set search_path = ''
as $$
declare
  _updated integer;
begin
  update public.mod_notifications n
     set read_at = now()
   where n.user_id = (select auth.uid())
     and n.read_at is null;
  get diagnostics _updated = row_count;
  return _updated;
end;
$$;

sql:
-- Scheduler health for "Finish connecting your services" (/cms-setup/services,
-- /api/health/setup). Background work runs on Supabase Cron and needs no
-- CRON_SECRET: the runtime bootstrap stores the app URL + a derived cron
-- secret in Vault. What can still go wrong is the app not having booted
-- against this database yet, or Supabase not reaching the app — this reports
-- both. Service role only.
--
-- Append-only + idempotent-friendly.

create or replace function public.kit_scheduler_status()
returns jsonb
language sql
stable
security definer
set search_path = ''
as $$
  select jsonb_build_object(
    'jobs', (select count(*) from cron.job j where j.active),
    'app_url', exists (select 1 from vault.decrypted_secrets s where s.name = 'kit_app_url'),
    'cron_secret', exists (select 1 from vault.decrypted_secrets s where s.name = 'kit_cron_secret'),
    -- pg_net keeps responses for ~6 hours: recent enough to judge reachability.
    'last_ok_at', (
      select max(r.created) from net._http_response r
      where r.status_code between 200 and 299
    ),
    'last_failure_at', (
      select max(r.created) from net._http_response r
      where r.status_code is null or r.status_code >= 400
    ),
    'last_failure', (
      select coalesce(r.error_msg, 'HTTP ' || r.status_code::text)
      from net._http_response r
      where r.status_code is null or r.status_code >= 400
      order by r.created desc
      limit 1
    )
  );
$$;

name: mod_notifications_006_token_compat
sql:
-- Notifications 1.3.1 · keep already-installed mobile apps registering.
--
-- 004 made push tokens unique per device and dropped the (user_id, token)
-- unique key. Mobile builds already on people's phones still register with
-- `upsert(..., { onConflict: "user_id,token" })`, and Postgres rejects an ON
-- CONFLICT that names columns without a matching unique key — so those apps
-- could no longer register. Updates must keep the previous release's clients
-- working (expand/contract; tooling/mod/src/migration-safety.ts), so:
--   * the (user_id, token) key is back (token alone stays unique);
--   * a trigger moves a device's token to whoever registers it, for old and
--     new clients alike (the new app calls
--     mod_notifications_register_push_token, which does the same).
--
-- Reattach-friendly (if not exists / or replace).

do $$
begin
  if not exists (
    select 1 from pg_constraint
    where conname = 'mod_notifications_push_tokens_user_id_token_key'
  ) then
    alter table public.mod_notifications_push_tokens
      add constraint mod_notifications_push_tokens_user_id_token_key
      unique (user_id, token);
  end if;
end;
$$;

create or replace function public.mod_notifications_push_token_claim()
returns trigger
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = ''
as $$
begin
  -- RLS would hide another user's row from the caller; this runs as owner.
  delete from public.mod_notifications_push_tokens t
  where t.token = new.token and t.user_id is distinct from new.user_id;
  return new;
end;
$$;

drop trigger if exists mod_notifications_push_token_claim
  on public.mod_notifications_push_tokens;
create trigger mod_notifications_push_token_claim
  before insert on public.mod_notifications_push_tokens
  for each row execute function public.mod_notifications_push_token_claim();

sql:
-- Notifications 1.4 · push reliability.
--
-- 1. mod_notifications_push_tickets — the Expo push ticket ids the dispatcher
--    got back from each send (id + the token it went to; no message content).
--    The `push-receipts` Payload task reads them ~15 minutes later, fetches
--    Expo's receipts, removes tokens whose device is no longer registered
--    (`DeviceNotRegistered`), then deletes the processed tickets. Expo drops
--    receipts after 24 hours, so older tickets are deleted unread.
--    Server-only: RLS on, no policies (only the service role, which bypasses
--    RLS, reads or writes it).
-- 2. mod_notifications_unregister_push_token(_token) — the mobile app calls it
--    on sign-out so a device stops receiving the signed-out account's pushes.
--    Deletes only the caller's own row.
--
-- Append-only + idempotent-friendly.

-- ============================================================================
-- 1. Push tickets (server-only)
-- ============================================================================

create table if not exists public.mod_notifications_push_tickets (
  id text primary key, -- Expo push ticket id (receipt id)
  token text not null, -- the Expo push token the message was sent to
  created_at timestamptz not null default now()
);
create index if not exists mod_notifications_push_tickets_created_idx
  on public.mod_notifications_push_tickets (created_at);

-- Server-only ledger: RLS on, no policies (service role bypasses RLS).
alter table public.mod_notifications_push_tickets enable row level security;

-- ============================================================================
-- 2. Unregister this device on sign-out
-- ============================================================================

create or replace function public.mod_notifications_unregister_push_token(
  _token text
)
returns void
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = ''
as $$
begin
  if (select auth.uid()) is null then
    raise exception 'not allowed' using errcode = '42501';
  end if;
  delete from public.mod_notifications_push_tokens t
  where t.user_id = (select auth.uid())
    and t.token = _token;
end;
$$;

name: staff_workspaces
sql:
-- staff_workspaces: the list behind the header workspace switcher
-- (docs/WORKSPACES.md → Staff workspace view).
--
-- Staff aren't members of their customers' workspaces, and memberships /
-- organizations are member-scoped under RLS, so staff need a narrow,
-- read-only door: every workspace's id, name, slug, logo and member count.
-- Nothing else (no member names, no invite state). The switcher only scopes
-- the UI; each module's own staff policies still decide what staff can read.

create or replace function public.staff_workspaces(
  _q text default null,
  _limit integer default 50,
  _ids uuid[] default null
)
returns table (
  id uuid,
  name text,
  slug text,
  logo_url text,
  member_count integer
)
language plpgsql
stable
security definer
set search_path = ''
as $$
begin
  if (select auth.uid()) is null
     or public.is_anonymous_session()
     or not coalesce(
       (select p.is_staff from public.profiles p where p.id = (select auth.uid())),
       false
     ) then
    raise exception 'staff_workspaces: staff only' using errcode = '42501';
  end if;

  return query
    select
      o.id,
      o.name,
      o.slug,
      o.logo_url,
      (select count(*)::integer from public.memberships m where m.org_id = o.id)
    from public.organizations o
    where (_ids is null or o.id = any (_ids))
      and (
        nullif(btrim(coalesce(_q, '')), '') is null
        or o.name ilike '%' || btrim(_q) || '%'
        or o.slug ilike '%' || btrim(_q) || '%'
      )
    order by lower(o.name), o.id
    limit least(greatest(coalesce(_limit, 50), 1), 200);
end;
$$;

revoke execute on function public.staff_workspaces(text, integer, uuid[]) from public, anon;

name: mod_billing_005_provider_neutral
sql:
-- Billing 2.0 · provider-neutral billing core.
--
-- Billing used to be Stripe through and through. It is now a core that any
-- payment provider plugs into through an adapter module (Stripe today via
-- billing-adapter-stripe; an in-app purchase provider such as RevenueCat
-- later). One user may hold purchases from several providers at once, so the
-- ledger gains a `provider` everywhere and entitlements are read from one
-- view, whatever sold them:
--
--   * `provider` on customers/products/prices/subscriptions/webhook events
--     (existing rows are Stripe's);
--   * mod_billing_customer_links: one customer id per (user, provider) — the
--     old mod_billing_customers allows one per user, so it stays as Stripe's
--     legacy mirror until a later contract release;
--   * subscriptions gain what entitlements and tags need regardless of
--     provider: kind (subscription | one_time), plan_id (the Payload plan),
--     entitlement, store (web | app_store | play_store | promotional),
--     environment, provider_event_at (the ordering guard, provider-neutral);
--   * mod_billing_entitlements: the active rows, read under the caller's RLS
--     (security_invoker) — usePremium, the server entitlement check and the
--     paywall all read it;
--   * mod_billing_managed_tags: which public.tags billing keeps in sync (plan,
--     status, billing cycle, store) so reconciling never touches staff tags;
--   * mod_billing_claim_event(): the webhook claim, per provider;
--   * the hourly webhook check moves to the Stripe adapter (it registers its
--     own schedule); a daily billing-tags sweep is added.
--
-- Expand-only: every column is nullable or defaulted, the old functions keep
-- their signatures (the previous release's code still calls them), and the
-- Stripe-named columns stay until a later `-- dream:contract` release.
-- Reattach-friendly (if not exists / or replace).

alter table public.mod_billing_customers
  add column if not exists provider text not null default 'stripe';
alter table public.mod_billing_products
  add column if not exists provider text not null default 'stripe';
alter table public.mod_billing_prices
  add column if not exists provider text not null default 'stripe';
alter table public.mod_billing_webhook_events
  add column if not exists provider text not null default 'stripe';

alter table public.mod_billing_subscriptions
  add column if not exists provider text not null default 'stripe',
  add column if not exists kind text not null default 'subscription'
    check (kind in ('subscription', 'one_time')),
  add column if not exists plan_id text,
  add column if not exists entitlement text not null default 'premium'
    check (entitlement in ('members', 'premium')),
  add column if not exists store text not null default 'web'
    check (store in ('web', 'app_store', 'play_store', 'promotional')),
  add column if not exists environment text
    check (environment in ('live', 'test', 'sandbox')),
  add column if not exists provider_event_at timestamptz;

-- Lifetime purchases were written as an active row keyed by the Checkout
-- Session id (cs_…).
update public.mod_billing_subscriptions
  set kind = 'one_time'
  where id like 'cs\_%' and kind = 'subscription';
update public.mod_billing_subscriptions
  set provider_event_at = stripe_event_at
  where provider_event_at is null and stripe_event_at is not null;

create index if not exists mod_billing_subscriptions_user_status_idx
  on public.mod_billing_subscriptions (user_id, status);

-- One provider customer per (user, provider).
create table if not exists public.mod_billing_customer_links (
  user_id uuid not null references public.profiles (id) on delete cascade,
  provider text not null,
  provider_customer_id text not null,
  -- The wallet / checkout email when it differs from the account email.
  billing_email text,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  updated_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  primary key (user_id, provider),
  unique (provider, provider_customer_id)
);

alter table public.mod_billing_customer_links enable row level security;

drop policy if exists "mod_billing_customer_links: select own"
  on public.mod_billing_customer_links;
create policy "mod_billing_customer_links: select own"
  on public.mod_billing_customer_links for select to authenticated
  using (user_id = (select auth.uid()));

insert into public.mod_billing_customer_links
  (user_id, provider, provider_customer_id, billing_email, created_at)
select c.user_id, 'stripe', c.stripe_customer_id, c.billing_email, c.created_at
from public.mod_billing_customers c
on conflict do nothing;

-- Active entitlements, whatever sold them. security_invoker: the caller's
-- RLS on mod_billing_subscriptions applies (read-own).
create or replace view public.mod_billing_entitlements
  with (security_invoker = true)
as
select
  s.user_id,
  s.entitlement,
  s.provider,
  s.store,
  s.kind,
  s.status,
  s.id as subscription_id,
  s.price_id,
  s.plan_id,
  s.cancel_at_period_end,
  s.current_period_end as expires_at
from public.mod_billing_subscriptions s
where s.status in ('active', 'trialing');

-- Tags billing keeps in sync (see src/server/core/tags.ts). Server-only.
create table if not exists public.mod_billing_managed_tags (
  tag_id uuid primary key references public.tags (id) on delete cascade,
  tag_group text not null
    check (tag_group in ('plan', 'status', 'cycle', 'store')),
  value text not null,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now()
);
alter table public.mod_billing_managed_tags enable row level security;

-- Adopt the tags billing wrote before 2.0: "Free" (signup) and plan names
-- (Stripe product names), so the sync can remove them when they go stale.
insert into public.mod_billing_managed_tags (tag_id, tag_group, value)
select t.id, 'status', 'free'
from public.tags t
where t.name = 'Free' and t.is_system
on conflict (tag_id) do nothing;
insert into public.mod_billing_managed_tags (tag_id, tag_group, value)
select t.id, 'plan', t.name
from public.tags t
join public.mod_billing_products p on p.name = t.name
where t.is_system
on conflict (tag_id) do nothing;

-- Same body as 003's, extended with the 2.0 columns (all optional in _row,
-- so the previous release's callers keep working) and the provider-neutral
-- ordering stamp.
create or replace function public.mod_billing_apply_subscription(
  _row jsonb,
  _event_at timestamptz
)
returns boolean
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = ''
as $$
declare
  _applied boolean;
  _provider text := coalesce(_row ->> 'provider', 'stripe');
begin
  if coalesce((select auth.role()), '') in ('authenticated', 'anon') then
    raise exception 'mod_billing_apply_subscription: not allowed' using errcode = '42501';
  end if;
  -- The subscription may arrive before its price (providers don't order
  -- events): keep a stub so the foreign key holds; the catalog sync fills it.
  if _row ->> 'price_id' is not null then
    insert into public.mod_billing_prices (id, active, provider)
    values (_row ->> 'price_id', true, _provider)
    on conflict (id) do nothing;
  end if;
  insert into public.mod_billing_subscriptions as s (
    id, user_id, price_id, status, quantity, cancel_at_period_end,
    current_period_end, stripe_event_at, provider_event_at, updated_at,
    provider, kind, plan_id, entitlement, store, environment
  )
  values (
    _row ->> 'id',
    (_row ->> 'user_id')::uuid,
    _row ->> 'price_id',
    _row ->> 'status',
    (_row ->> 'quantity')::integer,
    coalesce((_row ->> 'cancel_at_period_end')::boolean, false),
    (_row ->> 'current_period_end')::timestamptz,
    case when _provider = 'stripe' then _event_at end,
    _event_at,
    now(),
    _provider,
    coalesce(_row ->> 'kind', 'subscription'),
    _row ->> 'plan_id',
    coalesce(_row ->> 'entitlement', 'premium'),
    coalesce(_row ->> 'store', 'web'),
    _row ->> 'environment'
  )
  on conflict (id) do update
    set user_id = excluded.user_id,
        price_id = excluded.price_id,
        status = excluded.status,
        quantity = excluded.quantity,
        cancel_at_period_end = excluded.cancel_at_period_end,
        current_period_end = excluded.current_period_end,
        stripe_event_at = excluded.stripe_event_at,
        provider_event_at = excluded.provider_event_at,
        provider = excluded.provider,
        kind = excluded.kind,
        plan_id = coalesce(excluded.plan_id, s.plan_id),
        entitlement = excluded.entitlement,
        store = excluded.store,
        environment = coalesce(excluded.environment, s.environment),
        updated_at = now()
    where coalesce(s.provider_event_at, s.stripe_event_at) is null
       or excluded.provider_event_at is null
       or excluded.provider_event_at >= coalesce(s.provider_event_at, s.stripe_event_at)
  returning true into _applied;
  return coalesce(_applied, false);
end;
$$;

-- The webhook claim, per provider (see 004 for the semantics). Stripe event
-- ids stay bare (evt_…), so a delivery claimed by the previous release is
-- still recognized; other providers' ids are stored as "<provider>:<id>".
create or replace function public.mod_billing_claim_event(
  _provider text,
  _id text,
  _type text
)
returns text
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = ''
as $$
declare
  _key text := case when _provider = 'stripe' then _id else _provider || ':' || _id end;
  _status text;
begin
  if coalesce((select auth.role()), '') in ('authenticated', 'anon') then
    raise exception 'mod_billing_claim_event: not allowed' using errcode = '42501';
  end if;
  for _i in 1..2 loop
    insert into public.mod_billing_webhook_events (id, type, status, claimed_at, provider)
    values (_key, _type, 'processing', now(), _provider)
    on conflict (id) do nothing;
    if found then
      return 'claimed';
    end if;

    update public.mod_billing_webhook_events e
      set claimed_at = now(), received_at = now()
    where e.id = _key
      and e.status = 'processing'
      and (e.claimed_at is null or e.claimed_at < now() - interval '5 minutes');
    if found then
      return 'claimed';
    end if;

    select e.status into _status
    from public.mod_billing_webhook_events e
    where e.id = _key;
    if _status = 'done' then
      return 'duplicate';
    end if;
    if _status = 'processing' then
      return 'busy';
    end if;
  end loop;
  return 'busy';
end;
$$;

-- Finish a claim: 'done' after the side effects ran, or released (deleted)
-- so the provider's retry can run them.
create or replace function public.mod_billing_finish_event(
  _provider text,
  _id text,
  _ok boolean
)
returns void
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = ''
as $$
declare
  _key text := case when _provider = 'stripe' then _id else _provider || ':' || _id end;
begin
  if coalesce((select auth.role()), '') in ('authenticated', 'anon') then
    raise exception 'mod_billing_finish_event: not allowed' using errcode = '42501';
  end if;
  if _ok then
    update public.mod_billing_webhook_events set status = 'done' where id = _key;
  else
    delete from public.mod_billing_webhook_events
    where id = _key and status = 'processing';
  end if;
end;
$$;

sql:
-- Billing 2.1 · workspace-owned plans and staff grants.
--
--   * A purchase can belong to a WORKSPACE (org_id): the company pays, every
--     member gets the entitlement, owners/admins manage it. user_id stays the
--     person who bought it (or, for a staff grant, the workspace owner).
--   * Members read their workspace's purchases (the one SELECT policy now
--     covers own OR workspace rows; one permissive policy per action keeps
--     the advisors quiet), so mod_billing_entitlements — security_invoker —
--     lists workspace entitlements to every member automatically.
--   * mod_billing_org_customer_links: one provider customer per (workspace,
--     provider); readable by the workspace's owners/admins.
--   * Staff grants ("comp" plans): rows with provider 'manual', store
--     'promotional', plus who granted them and why. A grant with an end date
--     stops counting once it passes (the view checks; the daily billing-tags
--     run marks it canceled).
--
-- Expand-only; mod_billing_apply_subscription keeps its signature (new keys
-- in _row are optional). Reattach-friendly.

alter table public.mod_billing_subscriptions
  add column if not exists org_id uuid
    references public.organizations (id) on delete cascade,
  add column if not exists granted_by uuid
    references public.profiles (id) on delete set null,
  add column if not exists note text;

create index if not exists mod_billing_subscriptions_org_idx
  on public.mod_billing_subscriptions (org_id)
  where org_id is not null;
create index if not exists mod_billing_subscriptions_granted_by_idx
  on public.mod_billing_subscriptions (granted_by)
  where granted_by is not null;

drop policy if exists "mod_billing_subscriptions: select own"
  on public.mod_billing_subscriptions;
drop policy if exists "mod_billing_subscriptions: select own or workspace"
  on public.mod_billing_subscriptions;
create policy "mod_billing_subscriptions: select own or workspace"
  on public.mod_billing_subscriptions for select to authenticated
  using (
    user_id = (select auth.uid())
    or org_id = any (array(select private.user_org_ids()))
  );

create table if not exists public.mod_billing_org_customer_links (
  org_id uuid not null references public.organizations (id) on delete cascade,
  provider text not null,
  provider_customer_id text not null,
  billing_email text,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  updated_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  primary key (org_id, provider),
  unique (provider, provider_customer_id)
);

alter table public.mod_billing_org_customer_links enable row level security;

drop policy if exists "mod_billing_org_customer_links: select workspace admins"
  on public.mod_billing_org_customer_links;
create policy "mod_billing_org_customer_links: select workspace admins"
  on public.mod_billing_org_customer_links for select to authenticated
  using (org_id = any (array(select private.user_admin_org_ids())));

-- Entitlements now include workspace purchases (through RLS) and drop staff
-- grants whose end date has passed. Columns are appended, never reordered.
create or replace view public.mod_billing_entitlements
  with (security_invoker = true)
as
select
  s.user_id,
  s.entitlement,
  s.provider,
  s.store,
  s.kind,
  s.status,
  s.id as subscription_id,
  s.price_id,
  s.plan_id,
  s.cancel_at_period_end,
  s.current_period_end as expires_at,
  s.org_id
from public.mod_billing_subscriptions s
where s.status in ('active', 'trialing')
  and (
    s.provider <> 'manual'
    or s.current_period_end is null
    or s.current_period_end > now()
  );

-- 005's function, plus org_id / granted_by / note (all optional in _row).
create or replace function public.mod_billing_apply_subscription(
  _row jsonb,
  _event_at timestamptz
)
returns boolean
language plpgsql
security definer
set search_path = ''
as $$
declare
  _applied boolean;
  _provider text := coalesce(_row ->> 'provider', 'stripe');
begin
  if coalesce((select auth.role()), '') in ('authenticated', 'anon') then
    raise exception 'mod_billing_apply_subscription: not allowed' using errcode = '42501';
  end if;
  if _row ->> 'price_id' is not null then
    insert into public.mod_billing_prices (id, active, provider)
    values (_row ->> 'price_id', true, _provider)
    on conflict (id) do nothing;
  end if;
  insert into public.mod_billing_subscriptions as s (
    id, user_id, price_id, status, quantity, cancel_at_period_end,
    current_period_end, stripe_event_at, provider_event_at, updated_at,
    provider, kind, plan_id, entitlement, store, environment,
    org_id, granted_by, note
  )
  values (
    _row ->> 'id',
    (_row ->> 'user_id')::uuid,
    _row ->> 'price_id',
    _row ->> 'status',
    (_row ->> 'quantity')::integer,
    coalesce((_row ->> 'cancel_at_period_end')::boolean, false),
    (_row ->> 'current_period_end')::timestamptz,
    case when _provider = 'stripe' then _event_at end,
    _event_at,
    now(),
    _provider,
    coalesce(_row ->> 'kind', 'subscription'),
    _row ->> 'plan_id',
    coalesce(_row ->> 'entitlement', 'premium'),
    coalesce(_row ->> 'store', 'web'),
    _row ->> 'environment',
    (_row ->> 'org_id')::uuid,
    (_row ->> 'granted_by')::uuid,
    _row ->> 'note'
  )
  on conflict (id) do update
    set user_id = excluded.user_id,
        price_id = excluded.price_id,
        status = excluded.status,
        quantity = excluded.quantity,
        cancel_at_period_end = excluded.cancel_at_period_end,
        current_period_end = excluded.current_period_end,
        stripe_event_at = excluded.stripe_event_at,
        provider_event_at = excluded.provider_event_at,
        provider = excluded.provider,
        kind = excluded.kind,
        plan_id = coalesce(excluded.plan_id, s.plan_id),
        entitlement = excluded.entitlement,
        store = excluded.store,
        environment = coalesce(excluded.environment, s.environment),
        org_id = coalesce(excluded.org_id, s.org_id),
        granted_by = coalesce(excluded.granted_by, s.granted_by),
        note = coalesce(excluded.note, s.note),
        updated_at = now()
    where coalesce(s.provider_event_at, s.stripe_event_at) is null
       or excluded.provider_event_at is null
       or excluded.provider_event_at >= coalesce(s.provider_event_at, s.stripe_event_at)
  returning true into _applied;
  return coalesce(_applied, false);
end;
$$;

-- Feedback module · Autopilot (AI triage, Canny's Autopilot).
--
-- The cron processes new posts once (ai_processed_at): embeds them, files
-- them into a category, and suggests duplicates in the staff inbox (or, in
-- "automated" mode, merges portal duplicates as votes, logged with undo).
-- Feedback from other sources (the inbound API, the chat adapter) lands in
-- the same inbox and becomes a post only when staff accept it — internal by
-- default, as in Canny. Everything is staff-only.

alter table public.mod_feedback_posts
  add column if not exists embedding extensions.vector(1536),
  add column if not exists ai_processed_at timestamptz,
  add column if not exists summary text,
  add column if not exists summary_comment_count integer;

create index if not exists mod_feedback_posts_embedding_idx
  on public.mod_feedback_posts using hnsw (embedding extensions.vector_cosine_ops);
create index if not exists mod_feedback_posts_unprocessed_idx
  on public.mod_feedback_posts (created_at)
  where ai_processed_at is null and deleted_at is null;

create table if not exists public.mod_feedback_inbox (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  -- duplicate (post ↔ post) | extracted (raw feedback from a source)
  kind text not null check (kind in ('duplicate', 'extracted')),
  source text not null default 'portal',
  -- For duplicates: the new post; for extracted feedback: null until accepted.
  post_id uuid references public.mod_feedback_posts (id) on delete cascade,
  suggested_post_id uuid references public.mod_feedback_posts (id) on delete set null,
  suggested_board_id text references public.mod_feedback_boards (id) on delete set null,
  suggested_category_id text references public.mod_feedback_categories (id) on delete set null,
  title text,
  raw_text text,
  author_email text,
  author_name text,
  origin_ref jsonb not null default '{}'::jsonb,
  confidence real,
  state text not null default 'pending'
    check (state in ('pending', 'accepted', 'merged', 'dismissed')),
  resolved_by uuid references public.profiles (id) on delete set null,
  resolved_at timestamptz,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now()
);

  on public.mod_feedback_inbox (created_at desc) where state = 'pending';
create index if not exists mod_feedback_inbox_post_idx on public.mod_feedback_inbox (post_id);
create index if not exists mod_feedback_inbox_suggested_idx on public.mod_feedback_inbox (suggested_post_id);
create index if not exists mod_feedback_inbox_board_idx on public.mod_feedback_inbox (suggested_board_id);

drop policy if exists "mod_feedback_inbox: staff" on public.mod_feedback_inbox;

  on public.mod_feedback_inbox for all to authenticated

  with check ((select public.mod_feedback_is_staff()));

alter table public.mod_feedback_api_keys enable row level security;

drop policy if exists "mod_feedback_api_keys: staff read" on public.mod_feedback_api_keys;
create policy "mod_feedback_api_keys: staff read"
  on public.mod_feedback_api_keys for select to authenticated
  using ((select public.mod_feedback_is_staff()));

-- Nearest posts by meaning (invoker: only readable posts come back).
create or replace function public.mod_feedback_similar_by_embedding(
  _embedding extensions.vector(1536),
  _board text default null,
  _exclude uuid default null,
  _limit integer default 5
)
returns table (
  id uuid,
  board_id text,
  slug text,
  title text,
  details text,
  status_id text,
  vote_count integer,
  comment_count integer,
  similarity real
)
language sql
stable
set search_path = ''
as $$
  select p.id, p.board_id, p.slug, p.title, left(p.details, 300), p.status_id,
         p.vote_count, p.comment_count,
         (1 - extensions.cosine_distance(p.embedding, _embedding))::real
  from public.mod_feedback_posts p
  where p.embedding is not null
    and p.deleted_at is null
    and p.approval_state = 'approved'
    and p.merged_into_id is null
    and (_board is null or p.board_id = _board)
    and (_exclude is null or p.id <> _exclude)
  order by extensions.cosine_distance(p.embedding, _embedding)
  limit least(greatest(coalesce(_limit, 5), 1), 20);
$$;
